To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed an on-line, adaptive, scalable algorithm for computing page importance in a graph; (2) the algorithm is correct, and converges quickly, even for graphs that change dynamically; (3) we have implemented it, and used it to crawl the web.
(1) OPIC is a correct on-line page importance algorithm that requires much less resources than previous algorithms.
(a) OPIC is the first algorithm that is both on-line and adaptive; (b) OPIC converges quickly; and (c) Adaptive OPIC converges faster than OPIC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of on-line algorithms for computing page importance in a dynamic environment.
the development and evaluation of on-line algorithms to compute page importance.
the development of efficient on-line algorithms for the computation of page importance and the use of these algorithms to focus web crawlers on the most important pages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OPIC algorithm works well and is very efficient.
OPIC is the best choice for the computation of page importance for the web, in particular for the purpose of focusing crawls.
OPIC is a good algorithm to use for computing page importance on-line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new algorithms work well and are very useful. They are now used by XYLEME.
we have shown that it is possible to compute page rank on-line and adaptively, using a small amount of resources.
the algorithms we propose have a very good performance, and that they are very well adapted to the web.
The main takeaway from our work is that
on-line algorithms are possible, and that on-line algorithms can be used to guide crawling to the most important pages.
the on-line algorithms can compute the same page importance as the off-line ones, and that they can do so using less resources and in a more flexible manner.
the use of a small number of pages visited on-line is sufficient to compute page importance with high accuracy, and that it can be done on-line.
